A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InterMimic and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A–H. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite citation renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, including baseline comparisons in Tables 1–2, ablations, zero-shot demonstrations, and supplementary failure and retargeting examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and qualitative simulation results, including the supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The teacher–student procedure, rewards, physical state initialization, interaction early termination, architectures, and PPO/DAgger training remain unchanged. The revised pose-joint count clarifies inclusion of the root; both versions retain 51 actuated joints and a 153-dimensional action space.

E1.justification: Both versions use OMOMO, BEHAVE, HODome, IMHD, and HIMO, with the same generation, prediction, novel-object, increased-object-weight, and retargeting scenarios. Newly identifying datasets through InterAct does not establish additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: PhysHOI remains the qualitative comparator, SkillMimic remains in Table 1, and the PPO, DAgger, and architectural comparisons in Table 2 are unchanged. Newly cited related work is not added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 4 refines the reported evaluation definitions: success requires successful imitation at least once, and tracking errors are averaged within the best-performing trial. Splits, sample counts, and other settings remain unchanged; these reporting revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The PSI/IET ablations, reference-distillation and PPO/DAgger comparisons, architecture comparison, and heavier-object test are retained. Supplementary initialization analysis, failure cases, and retargeting demonstrations also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies best-performing-trial selection for tracking-error summaries and success-at-least-once aggregation. This adds information about statistical summarization, but neither version supplies evaluation trial counts, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–2 match after accounting for spacing and citation numbering. For example, Table 1 retains InterMimic's 42.6 duration, 6.4 human error, and 9.2 object error. Qualitative findings and supplementary result examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the human-pose rotation and position dimensions from 51×3 to 52×3 and the non-hand joint count from 21 to 22. It specifies global coordinates for the root and parent-relative coordinates for other joints. Other mathematical formulations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable whole-body interaction control, teacher-based refinement, and zero-shot integration with generators. Section 2 emphasizes universal loco-manipulation more explicitly without changing the core contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distillation, RL fine-tuning, and Transformer performance remain unchanged. The appendices retain the same limitations concerning severe MoCap errors, penetration-based object support, fine finger dexterity, and humanoid deployment.

D1.justification: v2 adds root-versus-parent coordinate conventions, identifies InterAct as a dataset source, and acknowledges computing resources used. Supplementary hyperparameters and implementation procedures remain unchanged, as does the statement promising a future code release.

R1.justification: The literature survey is substantially narrowed, with references reduced from 197 to 114 and single-frame interaction coverage removed. v2 adds TokenHSI and InterAct, revises the closest-method discussion from single-hand grasping toward extending single-object skills, and removes explicit policy-distillation inspiration citations from Section 3.3.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted related-work rewrites, expands the pose and contact-inference explanations, refines metric wording, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and main and supplementary section structures remain intact.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained, with changes to equation spacing, text flow, and supplementary placement. Figure E moves to the opposite column and Figure F moves to the final supplementary page; visible page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical clarity by correcting the pose description and making success-at-least-once and best-trial reporting explicit, helping readers interpret the unchanged experiments. The narrower bibliography sacrifices breadth and some explicit methodological attribution, and trial counts remain unspecified. These tradeoffs limit the net benefit to a modest improvement.
